title: Using magnetic structure of Co40Pd60/Cu for the sensing of hydrogen
central_claims: A [Co40Pd60/Cu]10/Fe device shows reproducible hydrogen-dependent magnetic/electrical response, with roughly fivefold change at75kPa and about50% signal-to-noise restoration under1000Oe at0.7kPa.
Operando spectroscopy attributes the magnetic change to Co–Pd charge transfer coupled with local-symmetry changes.

source_manifest.title: Using magnetic structure of Co40Pd60/Cu for the sensing of hydrogen
source_manifest.finding: Institutional author record supplies full abstract and exact device, pressure, field and response claims; publisher and repository searches did not yield full original.

source_manifest.title: Magnetic gas sensing: working principles and recent developments
source_manifest.finding: Shinde and Rout explicitly retain the Co40Pd60/Cu fivefold magnetization/resistance response at75kPa in their review. Their concluding assessment also emphasizes unresolved stability, selectivity, interference and practical-application challenges.

source_manifest.title: Magneto-Electronic Hydrogen Gas Sensors: A Critical Review
source_manifest.finding: Maksymov and Kostylev survey competing magneto-electronic approaches and cite target; examined sections do not establish replication or commercialization of this particular stack.

source_manifest.title: Hydrogen-mediated magnetic domain formation and domain wall motion in Co30Pd70 alloy films
source_manifest.finding: Studies different Co30Pd70 films and cites target as prior sensor proof; Wen-Chin Lin overlaps original team. Magnetic response depends on composition and structure.

source_manifest.title: Hydrogenation Effect on Interlayer Coupling and Magneto-Transport Properties of Pd/Co/Mg/Fe Multilayers
source_manifest.finding: Uses Mg spacer for persistent hydrogenation and changed magnetotransport; same Lin collaborator, different device, not an independent test of original low-pressure sensing advantage.

source_manifest.title: Realization of an H2/CO dual-gas sensor using CoPd magnetic structures
source_manifest.finding: Original Liang/Lin/Tseng team extends CoPd research to dual-gas sensing and charge-transfer plus adsorption; available abstract does not establish the original Cu stack is reused.
